title: Staff engineer expectations: scope, influence and technical decisions
summary: A staff iOS engineer is judged on impact beyond their own code: setting technical direction, making good trade-off decisions, raising quality across teams and growing other engineers.
body: **What changes at staff level:** scope moves from "my feature" to "the iOS platform / several teams". Success is measured by outcomes for the org (velocity, quality, reliability), not lines of code.

**Typical staff responsibilities in iOS:** architecture and modularization direction; platform health (launch time, crash rate, build time, app size); design-system and shared SDKs; release process; Swift/SwiftUI adoption; cross-team technical reviews; incident leadership; mentoring senior engineers.

**Making decisions:** write RFCs/ADRs; compare 2-3 options with trade-offs (cost, risk, reversibility, team skills); prefer reversible decisions made quickly and invest more care in irreversible ones; disagree and commit.
**Influence without authority:** build trust with data and prototypes, listen first, find shared goals with product and design, give credit, make others successful.
**Raising the bar:** coding guidelines, code review culture, lint and CI checks, golden-path templates, documentation, tech talks.

**Behavioral question bank to prepare (with numbers):** a hard technical decision and its trade-offs; a time you were wrong; a conflict with another team; an incident you led; a project that failed; how you mentored someone to promotion; how you prioritized tech debt against features.
**Answer with STAR:** Situation, Task, Action (what **you** did), Result (measurable), Learning.
keyPoints: Impact beyond your team: direction, platform health, multiplying others.
Decisions documented in RFCs/ADRs with explicit trade-offs.
Influence through data, prototypes and trust.
Own platform metrics: crash-free rate, launch, hangs, build time, size.
mistakes: Answering behavioral questions with "we" only - interviewers need your specific actions.
Only technical depth, no evidence of cross-team influence.
followups: **How do you balance tech debt and features?** Tie debt to business impact (incidents, velocity), reserve a steady percentage of capacity, attach cleanup to feature work in the same area.
**How do you evaluate a new technology (e.g. TCA, SwiftData)?** Prototype on a real feature, define success criteria, assess team skills and lock-in, decide with an ADR, plan an exit path.
